response.answer:
The First Sentence Scribe
Fictional patent sketch.

FIGURE 1
```text
[A: quill pen — dips into ink perpetually]
                   ↓
[B: velvet scroll holder — unfurls a fresh start]
                   ↓
[C: time-sink hourglass — flips with each rewrite]
BACK TO A: the hourglass's final grain triggers a new dip
```

CLAIM 1 — An apparatus for converting the initial spark of an idea into an endless loop of preliminary drafting, while ensuring the core narrative remains perpetually unwritten.

BENCH TEST — In this imagined study, the operator picks up the quill. The velvet scroll holder unfurls a pristine sheet, and the scribe dips the pen, ready to begin. The operator writes a single sentence, then pauses. The time-sink hourglass flips, its last grain falling. This triggers the quill to dip again, presenting a fresh, blank scroll, and the operator, compelled by the new beginning, rewrites the first sentence.

REMOVE ONE PART
A: Lose the perpetual ink dip; gain the ability to stop writing, but the operator must manually reload the pen.
B: Lose the fresh scroll unfurler; gain the visibility of previous drafts, but the operator must manually select a new page.
C: Lose the time-sink hourglass; gain the ability to write without the immediate pressure of time passing, but the operator must manually track the elapsed writing time.

Try outside the sketch: before dipping the pen, state one concrete detail the next sentence will introduce.
